text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironment“Medium Roast, Cream, No Plastic”: New Coffee Cup Coating Protects Against MicroplasticsAnd makes recycling a breezeJCBy Jake Currie9:00 AM CST on November 9, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleYour paper coffee cup may be harboring a dangerous secret: a thin polyethylene lining. Sure, the plastic coating keeps your cup from getting soggy, but microplastics it sheds may end up in your body. By some estimates, Americans use roughly 136 million of these disposable cups each day. But because mixing paper and plastic is a recycling no-no, they may all wind up in a landfill. Now help may be on the way, according to a new paper published in ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering. Powered By 1053.2K 00ShareNextStayAfter their testing revealed polyethylene-coated cups experience surface degradation and particle release, a team of chemists from the University of Waterloo decided to make their own waterproof coating. The researchers developed a recipe for a plant-based protective barrier made of cellulose acetate infused with cellulose nanocrystals to provide sturdiness. Read more: “How Coffee Affects Your Sex Hormone Levels”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
